findings.description: `realpath` only follows a symlink when `canonicalize()` succeeds. `canonicalize()` fails when the link's target does not exist, so a dangling symlink stays unresolved and the hook tests the link's own path against `FROZEN_PATHS_REGEX`. The shell hook uses Python's `os.path.realpath`, which follows such a link to its target path, so it blocks a Write that the Rust port lets through.

The new `|| exit 2` turns any jq failure into a block, not only an unparseable payload. On a machine without jq, every Bash tool call is now blocked. The project's own convention says workers may lack jq and that hooks must fall back.
findings.body:
**On a machine without jq, `|| exit 2` now blocks every Bash call.**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/13615742b75a71b3186ede9a6fb105ee62505a32/.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh#L8-L10

```bash
COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty') || exit 2
```

The stated intent is to block a payload that jq cannot parse (exit 5). But `|| exit 2` catches every failure of that pipeline, including `jq: command not found` (127).
- **Before this PR:** `set -e` exited 127, which Claude Code treats as non-blocking, so the Bash call ran.
- **Now:** the hook exits 2 on every Bash payload, whatever the command. `.claude/settings.json` at HEAD runs this hook on PreToolUse `matcher: "Bash"`, so this is live today, not waiting for the Rust wiring.

The block also prints no `BLOCKED:` reason, only bash's `jq: command not found`, unlike every other exit 2 in the script. The Rust port has the same gap: `tools/hooks-rs/src/git_safety.rs:10` exits 2 on an unreadable payload with no message.

The repo expects this trigger. `.claude/skills/ci-and-agent-config/SKILL.md` §2 Portability says: "`jq` may be missing on a worker machine. A hook that parses its JSON payload falls back without it, as `push-gate.sh` does."

The PR's declared change covers an unparseable payload. It does not cover a missing jq.

**Fix:** guard the jq call with `command -v jq` and fall back to the raw payload, as `push-gate.sh` does. Add a `BLOCKED:` line before the exit so the agent sees why.
findings.suggestion:
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # jq exits 5 on a payload it cannot parse, which Claude Code treats as a
  # non-blocking error: only exit 2 stops the command.
  COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty') || { echo "BLOCKED: git-safety could not parse the hook payload" >&2; exit 2; }
else
  # Without jq the raw payload still carries the command's words, as in push-gate.sh.
  COMMAND=$INPUT
fi

findings.description: Test adequacy: the declared non-JSON behaviour is untested for three of the five hooks.
findings.body:
**Test adequacy: the declared exit-2-on-non-JSON behaviour of validate-file-naming is not pinned by any test.**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/13615742b75a71b3186ede9a6fb105ee62505a32/tools/hooks-rs/tests/path_guards.rs#L1-L154

The PR body lists one intentional difference: "`validate-file-naming` exits 2 on a payload that is not JSON where the shell exited 5". That behaviour is implemented at `src/validate_file_naming.rs:12` (`serde_json::from_str(&input).unwrap_or_else(|_| exit(2))`).

Every test in `path_guards.rs` sends a well-formed `json!` payload. If line 12 returned 0 on a parse failure, every test would still pass. Only `git_safety.rs:127-130` and `frozen_paths.rs:299-303` have a `blocks_payload_that_is_not_json` case.

`protect-generated` (`src/protect_generated.rs:9`, `payload().unwrap_or_default()`) and `tool-result-size` have no malformed-input case either. A case for each would pin their fail-open choice.

`docs/conventions/testing.md`: "Test behaviour through public interfaces."

findings.description: Test adequacy: the `.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh` change (`|| exit 2` on unparseable JSON) is covered by no shell harness.
findings.body:
**Test adequacy: no test exercises the one behaviour change that is live today.**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/13615742b75a71b3186ede9a6fb105ee62505a32/.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh#L10

The PR body says: "The one behaviour change today is `git-safety.sh` blocking on an unparseable payload." No test runs that script.
- `tests/hooks/` holds only `frozen-paths`, `push-gate`, `stop-hooks` and `tool-result-size`.
- Commit d84f8f2 added `tests/hooks/git-safety.test.sh` to run the same cases against both implementations. The file is gone at HEAD.
- The Rust `blocks_payload_that_is_not_json` (`tools/hooks-rs/tests/git_safety.rs:127-130`) calls `hook("git-safety")`, the binary, not the shell file.

You can delete `|| exit 2` and every test still passes.

The minimum fix is a `tests/hooks/git-safety.test.sh` case that pipes `not json` into the script and asserts exit 2. Restoring the dual-run harness from d84f8f2 also works. A no-jq case would also pin the correctness finding on the same line.

findings.description: If `regex_lite` cannot compile `(?i){FROZEN_PATHS_REGEX}`, the hook returns and allows the edit, with no message. Bash also allows on a regex that is invalid in both, so most of this mirrors the shell. The new part is a pattern that Bash's POSIX regex accepts but `regex_lite` rejects (for example a backreference): there the shell blocks and the Rust port allows, so the freeze is off without anyone being told. This also differs from `common::grep`, which exits 2 on a bad pattern. Blocking with a "FROZEN_PATHS_REGEX is not a valid regex" message would make a config mistake visible instead of disabling the freeze. In practice path regexes rarely use such features.

A payload holding an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escape (for example a lone \ud83d) makes serde_json::from_str fail, so tool-result-size returns silently with no warning. jq parses the same payload, replacing the half with U+FFFD, and warns. The likely trigger is Claude Code cutting a large Bash output (or a long Read line) with a JS string slice that lands inside an emoji's surrogate pair; JSON.stringify then writes the lone escape. Those are exactly the oversized results this hook exists to flag. The failure is quiet (the only cost is a lost advisory warning) and probably rare, and I have not checked Claude Code's truncation code. The same parse failure also reaches protect_generated.rs:9, which treats the payload as empty and so does not block (fails open), and validate_file_naming.rs:12, which exits 2 (fails closed). For those two a lone surrogate would have to sit in a model-written tool_input, which is close to unreachable. frozen_paths.rs:44 and git_safety.rs:10 parse the same way, outside this slice. One fix: before parsing, swap any `\uD800`-`\uDBFF` escape not followed by a low-surrogate escape (and any stray low surrogate) for `�`, as jq effectively does. Alternatively, accept the gap and record it as a declared difference.

When AGENT_FROZEN_ALLOW and FROZEN_PATHS_REGEX are both set, every Edit/Write spawns `git rev-parse --show-prefix` before the frozen regex is tried. That is one fork+exec, roughly 1-3 ms, on each edit, including edits to files that are nowhere near the frozen tree. A cheaper pre-filter is to match the regex against the typed path or a repo-relative path first, and spawn git only on a hit. The catch is that the code spawns git first on purpose, so a wrong-case parent directory is resolved to its on-disk case. A pre-filter would therefore need a case-insensitive match on the typed path, which over-approximates and is safe. The path only runs in sessions that set AGENT_FROZEN_ALLOW (worker sessions) and the cost is small, so it is optional.

The WHY comment for the `project.env` parsing is a `//` line inside the impl, attached to `load`, and it covers only quoting. The PR body states a second difference: values read as plain `KEY=value`, with no shell expansion. A reader of `Config::load` sees that difference only in the comment and not in a `///` doc, so the contract is easy to miss. It would be clearer as a `///` doc on `load`. `docs/conventions/core.md` §Comments: "Doc comments (docstrings, JSDoc, `///`): an imperative one-line summary is the contract." This is minor and guidance-grade.

This hook writes its own `BLOCKED:` message with three `eprintln!` calls and a manual `exit(2)`, while `common::block` (common.rs L8-11) already prints `BLOCKED: {message}` and exits 2, and three other modules use it. Folding the optional hint into one message and calling `block` keeps stderr and the exit code identical (about -9 +4 lines).

`opt-level = 3` under `[profile.release]` repeats Cargo's default for the release profile, so the line does nothing. Delete it (`-1`). The binary and the build flags stay the same; the other four keys (`lto`, `codegen-units`, `panic`, `strip`) change real defaults and stay.

The git-safety fail-open and edge paths are untested: no case runs without project.env (the `main` trunk fallback), outside a git repo or on a detached HEAD (where `on_trunk` returns false), with a payload missing `tool_input`, or with a trunk name holding regex metacharacters such as `release/1.0`.
No test covers `main.rs` dispatch of an unknown or missing subcommand, which exits 2 so that a wiring typo blocks rather than failing open. A `hook("nope")` case asserting exit 2 would pin it.

Two caller-reachable inputs are untested for frozen-paths: a payload with an empty or missing `file_path`, and a `project.env` line using `export` or double quotes (handled at `common.rs` line 64; only `path_guards.rs` exercises quoting).
No fail-open tests for `tool-result-size`: a missing `tool_response`, a non-object `tool_response` (a string), and a tool name other than Read, Edit or Bash, which should stay silent.

The shell guard hooks source `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/project.env` with `. file`, and hooks run outside the Bash sandbox. So any shell a sandboxed session writes into project.env runs unsandboxed the next time any session's hook fires. The same source line is in git-safety.sh L18, frozen-paths.sh L15, protect-generated.sh L7 and validate-file-naming.sh L17 (HEAD). The sandbox makes the repo cwd writable and I could not see whether its truncated deny list covers .claude/project.env, so confidence is medium. This PR's Rust port removes the sink: `Config::load` in tools/hooks-rs/src/common.rs L57-77 parses plain `KEY=value` and expands nothing. The fix lands when the next PR points settings.json at the binary.
